newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Soccer-Australian barred in row with Oceania.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Soccer-Australian barred in row with Oceania.

text.p: The Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) has suspended Australia's top soccer administrator as relations sour between the region's most powerful playing nation and its governing body.

OFC president Charlie Dempsey said on Wednesday Soccer Australia chairman David Hill had been barred from OFC meetings until February over his role in trying to block Oceania's elevation to full confederation status within world body FIFA.
He also cited what he described as disparaging personal remarks made against him and the confederation by Hill.
But Hill dismissed the move, describing the action as unconstitutional, unlawful and infantile.
In a recent Australian newspaper article, Hill described Dempsey as "Albert Steptoe" in a reference to the elderly, dishevelled junk-yard owner from a 1970s British comedy series.
"The unimpressive administration by the Dempsey fiefdom is retarding the development of soccer in the rest of the region," Hill told reporters on Wednesday.
"Given the current administration of the OFC my involvment is a waste of time," he said.
Australia angered their Pacific neighbours in July by opposing a FIFA motion to grant the region full confederation status, saying it lacked the strength to take on such a responsibility.
Hill, who led the campaign, cited the poor playing standards of other Oceania nations but lost the vote in Zurich by a crushing 172-1 margin.
Australia would prefer to play in the stronger Asian Football Confederation, a stance that particularly displeased Oceania neighbours Fiji and Tonga.
Speaking to Reuters in New Zealand, Dempsey said Hill had made some personal remarks about him that were not acceptable.
"It goes all the way back to when Australia opposed Oceania to get full membership of FIFA. It'a all been a saga. The least said, the sooner mended," Dempsey added.
After being informed of the OFC decision, Hill told reporters: "Frankly it's none of their business who Australia has as their representative to Oceania."

"This OFC meeting took place without Australia's involvement, so it is unconstitutional. Frankly it's unlawful....we wouldn't tell any other Oceania members who their representative should be," Hill said.
